content.text:
The test passes. Here's what I implemented.

## Summary

The change request — show the all-invoices list a page at a time (10 per page) with next/previous — is fundamentally presentational: the data is already fetched in one query, so pagination is "state that outlives a click," which per the app's conventions (rule 4) lives in the URL. No schema or server change was needed; forcing a migration/endpoint here would only add fragile coupling to a view-only concern.

I kept it additive:

1. **`features/invoices/pagination.ts`** (new) — defines `INVOICE_PAGE_SIZE = 10` and a `useInvoicePage()` hook that owns the `invoicePage` URL search param (1-based, defaults to page 1, clears the key on page 1 for a clean default URL).

2. **`features/invoices/pagination.slot.tsx`** (new) — a self-contained toolbar control filling the existing `allInvoices.toolbar` slot. It renders `invoice-page-prev`, `invoice-page-label`, and `invoice-page-next`. It queries invoices itself (and reads the shared `invoiceStatus` filter) to compute the last page, so Previous disables on page 1 and Next disables on the final page — sharing only the query key and URL keys with the list, never importing it.

3. **`features/invoices/AllInvoiceList.tsx`** (edited, same way the status filter was wired in) — reads the same `invoicePage` key and slices `shown` to the current 10-row window.

The two features coordinate purely through the shared `invoicePage` URL key and the `['invoices','all']` query key, matching the exact `data-testid` anchors the spec expects (`invoice-row-*`, `invoice-page-label`, `invoice-page-next`, `invoice-page-prev`). Typecheck and the Playwright spec both pass.
